subject.title: Crons ejecutaron mensajes de WhatsApp a la 1 AM fuera de horario y no se podían detener

question: Should the remaining emergency stop/delete behavior be solved by extending cron.remove or gateway stop to abort active outbound cron delivery, by adding a separate emergency stop command, or by treating task cancellation plus the restart replay fix as sufficient?
rationale: The restart replay subset has an open implementation candidate, but aborting in-flight sends crosses cron runtime, task registry, gateway shutdown, and channel delivery ownership, so automation should not choose the permanent operator contract.

options.title: Land replay fix and design explicit emergency stop
options.body: Keep the restart catch-up activation boundary separate, then add a maintainer-approved emergency halt surface for outbound cron delivery if that is the desired product contract.

options.title: Make cron.remove abort active runs
options.body: Treat deleting a cron job as an immediate cancellation request for matching live cron task runs, with focused tests for active isolated runs and delivery suppression.

options.title: Accept task cancellation as the stop path
options.body: Close the emergency-stop portion after the replay fix lands if maintainers decide task cancellation is the supported operator path and cron.remove remains store-only.

recommendation.title: Land replay fix and design explicit emergency stop
recommendation.body: Keep the restart catch-up activation boundary separate, then add a maintainer-approved emergency halt surface for outbound cron delivery if that is the desired product contract.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent cron dispatch ownership and the land-ready review on the active schedule-activation PR make this the best available routing candidate.
